#3255. How to Set Up Alexa Wishlist Alerts for Black Friday and Cyber Monday

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

Amazon’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale has officially started—but keeping track of the best discounts yet to land and figuring out which deals are worthwhile can be a challenge. As an alternative, you can have Alexa give you a heads-up about deals on products you already know you want to purchase, so you don’t have to spend time sorting through the noise.

Then head to the Alexa mobile app and go to More in the top left (the three horizontal lines) > Settings > Notifications > Amazon Shopping and toggle on Deal Recommendations under the Shopping Recommendations options. This ensures you’ll receive notifications for items that appear in your shopping activity.

If Alexa finds an upcoming deal on something in your Saved for Later, your Wish List, or in your Shopping Cart, you’ll receive a pop-up alert on your Echo Show display or see a yellow light ring on your Echo speaker. You can also ask, “Alexa, what are my notifications?” to hear a list of deals it has compiled thus far. You can also say "Alexa, let me know when [product name] goes on sale."

Alexa can detect deals up to 24 hours in advance, so you can either ask it to remind you again when a deal starts or request that it buy the item when the deal goes live. Simply say, “Alexa, buy it for me,” and it’ll charge the default payment and send the item to the default delivery address on your account.

As Chris Harrison leaves the Bachelor Mansion behind for Fox Nation‘s The Vow, the dating show’s first eligible Christian is facing some judgment.

Jace Cates, the star of the new faith-based dating show, apologized for obliging contestant Sierra Wood’s request to “grab my ass” on the third episode “Enter Into Temptation.”

“I think it’s no secret that Sierra and I had an initial connection right from the beginning. And what doesn’t really get talked about is, that’s a long day of shooting, and when that moment happened with Sierra, it was at the end of the day. I was trying to be very intentional with every single girl that day,” he told the California Post. “And me and Sierra were having our moment, and it was a very romantic setting. I was in the moment with her when she made that request and I acted on it.” Related Stories News "You Can't Put A Cease & Desist On Love": Chris Harrison Talks About Returning To The Dating Scene With 'The Vow' News Chris Harrison Dating Show 'The Vow' Unveils Trailer

Cates added, “So, that’s where my mindset was. It’s just really difficult because you have your faith at the forefront and you have your intention at the forefront, and then you’re also trying to build a relationship with people you see a future with. I think I made a mistake in that moment. I was in there, I’m not perfect. And what I’m happy with is that I apologized to the women, I took accountability. And I tried to make sure they know I want to be respectful.” Watch on Deadline

Although they’d never met before, Cates and Wood are both members of Rose Church in Portland, Oregon, where he was asked if their pastors have seen the on-air moment. “They’re going to find out very soon if they haven’t seen the episode yet,” he said.

Harrison’s new dating show comes after he parted ways with the Bachelor franchise in June 2021, following his support for a contestant amid controversy over a racist photo she previously posted.

Warner Bros. previously hit The Vow with a cease-and-desist over alleged copyright and trademark infringement. “You can’t put a cease and desist on love,” Harrison told Deadline in response.

“I’ve been away for five years. There have been dozens of other dating shows. They’ve come after one very publicly. Is it a coincidence? I don’t think so,” he said. “On the flip side, there are many friends of ours on that show still, people I care about, and this business is hard. I don’t wish anybody to lose their jobs. There’s enough room for everybody to be successful.”

#3253. LiberNovo’s Black Friday sale takes up to 42% off ergonomic chairs

You can spend plenty of time getting your Mac, display, and desk just right. But what about the chair you use every day? Between typing, taking video calls, and leaning back to watch something, your position changes throughout the day. Your chair should be able to keep up.

That’s the idea behind LiberNovo’s ergonomic chairs, which combine support that moves with you and a choice of sizes, including the Maxis range for bigger and taller users. For Black Friday, LiberNovo is taking up to 42% off in the U.S., with chairs starting at $609 and offers running November 19–30.

Adjusting a chair for your desk is one thing. Keeping that support as you change position is another. LiberNovo’s Dynamic Support System links the neck support, backrest, armrests, and seat so they move together as you recline.

The Bionic FlexFit Backrest adds eight flexible panels that contour independently. Rather than relying on a single rigid backrest, the design lets different sections follow your back as you shift or turn. Once you’ve adjusted the chair to fit, the system is designed to maintain contact through those movements with fewer manual readjustments.

Both the Omni and Maxis families offer five recline positions: 105, 115, 125, 135, and 160 degrees. That gives you options for desk work, a more relaxed position for watching a video, and a deeper recline for a break.

A higher weight limit is only part of finding a chair that fits. Taller users also need enough seat depth, a headrest that reaches the right spot, and armrests with room to adjust.

The LiberNovo Maxis range addresses those details with a 52 cm seat depth, a wider backrest with a flared base, and an extended-travel headrest with 140 mm of vertical adjustment and 120 mm of front-to-back adjustment. Its armrests sit lower and offer a wider, longer adjustment range to accommodate larger builds.

LiberNovo recommends Maxis for users approximately 5 feet 10 inches to 6 feet 7 inches tall, with a maximum supported weight of 399 pounds. Maxis is certified to BIFMA X5.11. The seat cushion uses firmer support at the rear and a softer front edge, while a six-spring Controlled Recline System is designed to build resistance progressively as you lean back.

For a shallower seat, the Omni family offers 45 cm and 48 cm configurations. Choosing between the two families starts with fit, then comes down to which features you want.

There are three feature tiers in each family. Omni SE and Maxis Manual offer manually adjusted lumbar support, without a motor or battery. Both retain the flexible backrest, dynamic support, and five recline positions.

The Maxis Electric includes motorized lumbar adjustment and OmniStretch, a five-minute powered stretch sequence used in deep recline.

Omni Pro and Maxis Airflow add Active AirFlow seat ventilation. A fan draws air through the cushion to carry heat away, and an occupancy sensor pauses the fan when you stand up. These models also include a larger 3,000 mAh rechargeable battery.

LiberNovo’s warranty covers the frame and structural components for six years, and electronic components for two years.

U.S. Black Friday prices run from November 19 through November 30. Here’s how the chair-only Basic Bundles compare:

Bundles add another option. The Omni Pro Standard Bundle includes the chair and a footrest for $983. The Maxis Electric Premium Bundle includes the chair, a footrest, and an extra battery for $1,202, down from a listed MSRP of $2,086.

LiberNovo is also offering 30-day price protection on eligible purchases. U.S. gift tiers begin at $800 for a Mouse Pad, $1,000 for an Eco-Comfort three-piece gift set, and $1,200 for an Ergo-to-Go Travel Suite. Qualifying orders of $2,000, $3,000, or $4,000 receive an automatic additional saving of $60, $100, or $180, respectively, without a code.

U.S. shoppers can also choose Klarna Pay in 4 at 0% APR.

Ready to give your desk setup a more comfortable place to sit? Shop LiberNovo’s Black Friday sale to compare Omni and Maxis models, choose your fit, and explore the available bundles through November 30.

There’s an awful lot to love about the Nintendo Switch 2. It’s less toy-like than its (excellent) predecessor, has a 1080p screen (up from 720p), and it reaches 4K while docked. The problem? Your existing microSD card will be great for Switch 1 games, but Switch 2 games need faster storage via microSD Express cards.

These carry a premium, but the good news is that they’re seeing significant discounts for Black Friday.

UK gamers can save 15%, netting a 512GB card for £135.99 down from £159.99, while US Switch 2 owners can find an even bigger 24% discount, grabbing a SanDisk option for $98.99.

Switch 2 owners in the United States can save even more, with a 24% discount on this 512GB SanDisk microSD card.

Meanwhile, if you're a British reader, you can pick up this microSD Express card from Lexar, available at a 15% discount.

With so many games now too big for cartridges (leading to the controversial Game Key cards that are basically just a download key), it’s worth reiterating just how hefty some Switch 2 titles can be.

Launch titles like Street Fighter 6 and Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition came in at 60GB, but things have got progressively more storage-hungry from there.

NBA 2K26 is over 70GB, EA Sports FC 27 is 75GB, and WWE 2K26 is 86GB, while the two Final Fantasy VII Remake titles are around 90GB each. That’s on top of launches this year like The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition, Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave, and many more.

Honestly, the Switch 2 has grown to become a haven for great third-party titles, and even if you’ve not invested in fresh storage space, you’ll no doubt find it very welcome as more games arrive, like FromSoftware’s Duskbloods, Maneater 2, and Xenoblade Genesis in 2027.

#3250. WhatsApp is raising group chat limit to 1,500 participants

WhatsApp is gradually rolling out an increase to its group chat limit, allowing up to 1,500 participants to join in, instead of the previous 1,024 cap. Here are the details.

While there are exceptions, there are generally two kinds of WhatsApp users: those who hate group chats, and those who can’t seem to be in enough of them.

If you’re in the second category, you’re likely aware that WhatsApp has steadily increased the number of participants allowed in group chats over the years, jumping from 100 to 256 in 2016, then to 512 and, soon after, to 1,024 in 2022.

Now, as spotted by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is once again expanding that limit, raising the maximum number of participants in a group chat to 1,500.

According to the website, the new limit is rolling out to users on iOS and Android, though the rollout is gradual, meaning “not every account will see the higher limit immediately.”

WhatsApp is automatically updating existing groups to support the new limit. This means that admins do not need to take any action to unlock the higher capacity. As soon as the update becomes available to their accounts, their groups will support up to 1500 members. As a result, the update lets admins add up to 476 new members to their existing groups.

This rollout comes as WhatsApp has been working to make group chats easier to manage. Just last month, the company announced four new features, including the ability to pin messages indefinitely, share status updates within groups, filter conversations by mentions and replies, and share recent message history with new members after they join.

To read WABetaInfo’s full report, follow this link.

#3248. John Carpenter Reveals Robert Rodriguez Back In Running To Helm ‘Escape from New York’ Reimagining

After 45 years, John Carpenter is still finding the right director to break an old cult classic out of lockup.

Having recently tapped Zack Snyder to write and direct a reimagining of Escape from New York, Carpenter noted he’s been considering another candidate, despite being told Synder is “on fire” during a recent podcast appearance.

“He’s not anymore, but he’s trying to get back,” Carpenter said on the Dropping Names podcast. “We’ll see. He’s a nice man. I liked him.”

The comment came after Snyder’s The Last Photograph premiered at TIFF in September to poor reviews, mostly over the film’s excessive violence and offensive content. Additionally, his Rebel Moon films at Netflix were critically panned. Watch on Deadline

Carpenter added, “We have a backup: Robert Rodriguez wants to. He a new story he wants to do. So, we’ll see.”

Meanwhile, after co-writing and directing the original, Carpenter is returning to compose the score once again. “I demanded to be the composer … we’re gonna remake the score,” he noted.

Rodriguez was previously attached to a remake of Escape from New York in 2017, with the hunt for a director leading to several candidates over the years, including Radio Silence.

In Escape from New York, special forces operative-turned-prisoner Snake Plissken (Kurt Russell) has 24 hours to rescue the president of the United States from the island of Manhattan, which has been converted into the country’s only maximum security prison. The 1996 sequel Escape from L.A. followed.

#3247. The Best Amazon Prime Benefits You Probably Don't Know About

If you’re going to commit to an Amazon Prime membership, you might as well squeeze as much as you can out of the deal. And there's a good amount of juice to squeeze there. The price you pay for Amazon depends on many factors, but regardless of how much you're paying, it's worth it for most people (we've done the math).

If you're on the fence about signing up, consider that Amazon's Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale is underway, and the company is hosting some amazing tech deals. It's a great time to sell your soul—or take advantage of the 30-day free trial—and there's a lot more to your membership than just deals and free shipping.

The standard Prime membership costs $14.99 per month or $139 per year, but there are other tiers that some people might qualify for. For example, the Amazon Prime for Young Adults program allows young adults between the ages of 18 and 24 to get all of the Prime perks for half the cost—$7.49 per month or $69 annually.

I'll be the first to admit I didn't know all of the benefits that Amazon Prime offers to its members. There are a lot more perks than people think. Here are the most impressive ones (and check out the full list):

Fast free shipping on millions of items: Depending on where you live, shipping can take one or two days, and some even come on the same day for orders of $25 or more in most areas—and it’s always free (if being shipped by the Amazon store).

Select pre-ordered items can be delivered on their release date for free (for most areas).

The option to have items delivered inside your garage with a smart garage device (depending on where you live) for $1.99 per order, or for free if you combine it with Amazon Day delivery.

Earn rewards for future purchases when you select free no-rush shipping.

The option to have all your weekly orders delivered on a specific day, to reduce waste from boxes.

Amazon Prime Visa card: Cardholders get 5% back on Amazon, Whole Foods, Chase Travel, and other purchases. Prime members who use this card extensively can earn rewards that offset the cost of membership.

A Grubhub+ and Uber Eats membership, normally $9.99 per month, which gets you free delivery on eligible orders, lower service fees, exclusive deals, and other perks as long as you remain a Prime Member (it used to be only for a year). The Uber Eats membership gets you free delivery on eligible restaurants of $25 or more.

Sharing with family or friends: Amazon Family is the existing program for sharing Prime benefits, and it allows you to add separate profiles for one other adult who lives in the same household as the primary account holder, up to four teens, and up to four child accounts. This grants access to all the standard benefits, such as free delivery, Prime Video with ads, Prime Reading, third-party benefits like Grubhub, and access to audiobooks, e-books, certain games, and Amazon Music.

Amazon Health: Prime users get One Medical access for an additional $9 per month or $99 per year. Through your devices, you’ll have 24/7 access to on-demand virtual care, plus real-life access to primary care offices in a number of U.S. cities. It accepts most major health insurance plans, too.

Amazon Pharmacy: Access to free two-day delivery and other savings on medications.

Prime Video: Prime includes unlimited streaming of movies, TV shows, and Amazon Originals with ads, which normally costs $9 per month.

Amazon Music Prime: Access to Amazon's Spotify-esque music streaming service (not to be confused with Amazon's other music streaming subscriptions).

Amazon Luna: A cloud gaming platform that offers new free games every month, free downloadable PC games, content, a monthly Twitch channel subscription, and a free channel subscription on Twitch each month for Prime Members.

Amazon Photos: Unlimited photo storage plus 5 GBs for videos and other files (which extends to members of your Family Vault).

Prime Reading: Free access to a rotating selection of e-books and magazines for Kindle or Fire tablets and Kindle apps.

Amazon's First Reads: You get up to two free e-books every month from a curated list of books handpicked by editors.

#3244. These 14 New Features Are Coming to iOS 27.3

Apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov. 3. While this update isn't as large as iOS 27 proper, it's surprisingly feature-filled for a 0.3 update. This is only a beta, so anything could (and likely will) change before Apple officially launches the update. But, as it stands, iOS 27.3 tests 10 new features—including one feature the company trialed in the previous beta.

Technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program. But a word of warning: Betas can be temperamental, and could be risky. As such, I'd recommend avoiding the beta until Apple releases the public beta, which comes after a bit more testing to iron out larger issues. Either way, make sure to make a full backup of your iPhone to a Mac or PC first, as issues with the beta could result in permanent data loss.

The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the company's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID. While it works well enough for unlocking your iPhone, it's still an adjustment for those of us used to Face ID. With iOS 27.3, Apple is now testing face unlock for the Duo—not Face ID, mind you. The Duo's front camera doesn't have the tech required to power Face ID or its secure protocols. Instead, this feature simply unlocks your iPhone Duo with a face scan. In addition, your Duo will still require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. You can read more about this new feature here.

iOS 27.3 also comes with a new setting that lets you lock your iPhone Duo by closing it—as you would expect from, say, a laptop—or, dare I say, a flip phone? Currently, closing the Duo seamlessly transitions what's on the big screen to the smaller display, and you have to press the side button to lock the phone.

With watchOS 27, Apple released "Audio Intelligence," a new set of features for Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Audio Intelligence uses the watches' new S11 chip, along with on-device AI and cloud-based AI, to run new features, like Sound Recognition and Shazam (music recognition).

With iOS 27.3, however, the company is now officially testing the other two Audio Intelligence features it originally announced with watchOS 27. First, there's Live Rewind: By double-clicking the watch crown, you can pull up a transcript of the last 15 seconds of a conversation. Siri Recap, on the other hand, displays summaries of conversations you had that day, in case you need a refresher on any chats you might have otherwise forgotten about,

The company generated some controversy when it first announced these two Audio Intelligence features, since, on the surface, it sounds like these new Apple Watches are essentially spying on people all day long. According to Apple, however, that isn't really the case. The company says Audio Intelligence is private, and never records or stores any audio. No speakers are ever identified, and text results (both transcripts and summaries) are deleted automatically after a set period of time unless the user saves them to the Siri app. You can read more about how Audio Intelligence works here.

Despite their claims, I'm sure there will still be strong feelings surrounding these Audio Intelligence features. We'll have to see whether Apple can prove Live Rewind and Siri Recap aren't all that creepy throughout the iOS 27.3 beta process.

iOS 27.3 also introduces app actions for Siri AI. Apple is testing new abilities for Siri AI, including organizing files, planning events, or adding photos to albums. You could ask Siri to organize your Downloads folder, or delete files that haven't been opened in more than a year. You could ask Siri to find a coffee shop you went to last week, or to save an article to your Reading List in Safari. You could ask Siri to check your calendar and set up a time for an event based on when you're free. You can even ask the assistant to schedule, edit, or unsend messages.

For example, you could ask Siri AI to help you plan a trip with your friends. You could ask the AI to put together a themed playlist in Apple Music, schedule a message to a group about an upcoming trip, organize the websites you've been visiting in Safari into a tab group, and, after the trip, ask Siri to move your best photos to your favorites album. These new actions work in the following apps: Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. Developers can also add Siri AI app actions support to their own apps.

Apple started testing its new Health app with the iOS 27.2 beta, but pulled the redesign before the official release. Now, with iOS 27.3, the new app is back. The new Health app has a health dashboard for the first time, as well as new features like Health Age and movement assessments. It seems to be pulling from some popular competitor services, hopefully, for the better. For more on the new Health app, check out Lifehacker health editor Beth Skwarecki's explainer.

Continuing on the Health track, iOS 27.3 also introduces "Gym Strength." This is a new Fitness+ feature that offers a personalized four-week strength-training plan. You can customize these plans to meet your goals, experience level, and schedule, and they adapt as you progress. You'll get recommendations based on your experience with exercises, reps, and sets, including video demos for exercises. You can access Gym Strength on both iPhone and iPad, and Apple Watches are optional—though you can log your progress with the wearable if you have it.

Apple is also testing a new Siri AI feature in Safari, that gives the bot access to entire webpages, including the parts of the site that aren't on-screen. Say you want to know all the gluten-free options on a menu on a restaurant's website, but only a portion of the site is actually in view. You could ask Siri to read you the gluten-free options, and it would pull from the whole page, even though you can only see part of it.

Vertical tabs have been a favorite among browser aficionados, as they give you more screen real estate in your browser while keeping your tabs off the side. Apple hasn't made the jump—until now. This feature works with iPads running iPadOS 27.3 as well as Macs running macOS 27.3.

Another new Safari feature in testing is "Adaptive Dark Mode." This feature forces websites into a dark theme, if they don't have a native theme of their own. There are third-party apps that can do this, but this is the first time Apple has offered this feature built into Safari.

Apple is also testing new StandBy experiences with iOS 27.3, which were previously only available on the iPhone Duo. When you turn your iPhone sideways while plugged in, you'll find new Analog and Digital Clock faces with new customization options. There's also a new Photos face, with the option to pull images from Shared Albums.

"Reachability" pulls your iPhone's display down towards the bottom of the screen, so you can access items towards the top of the display with one hand. It's a useful feature for those of us with big iPhones, and now, there's no iPhone bigger than the Duo. With iOS 27.3, Apple is testing Reachability for its first foldable phone. It's a bit like the inverse of how Reachability currently works: You can swipe on the left or right side of your Duo's display to shift the other side of the screen towards your current position. If you're holding your Duo in your left hand, a swipe of the left side will pull the right side over to the left, and vice versa.

Apple is also rolling out new languages for Siri AI in iOS 27.3. Now, Apple's smart assistant supports Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish, and Norwegian.

If you have an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPad running iPadOS 27.3, you now have access to Siri Mode in Camera. As with iOS, you can open the Camera app on iPadOS to access Siri Mode, and ask Siri about your surroundings.

If you watch videos in Apple Podcasts, you can find them in more sources than the Podcasts app. With the new updates, you'll find these videos on Apple TV 4K, select smart TVs, your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and even in CarPlay. (Please don't watch video podcasts while driving.)

#3242. ‘Yellowjackets’ Creators On Ending Show Ahead Of Original Five-Season Plan: “We Chose To Try To Squeeze It In”

While many Yellowjackets fans are struggling to cope with the inevitable end, for its series creators, it was the right time to land the plane.

Discussing the fourth and final season with Deadline, Ashley Lyle and Bart Nickerson explained that they didn’t want to “run the risk of overstaying our welcome” with another season when they were reaching the conclusion “more rapidly.”

“We’d always said that we had pitched a five-season plan, but we’d always given the caveat that we felt like the show would tell us when it wanted to end, and just in the breaking of this story, it started to feel like we were sort of moving towards the end more rapidly,” explained Nickerson. “And so, then the decision kind of became, ‘OK, do we sort of squeeze a lot into Season 4 or run the risk of overstaying our welcome out of the fifth season?’ We chose to try to squeeze it in, and that ended up really just kind of working out nicely from our perspective.

“The show has always had to be very kind of efficient, with the storytelling. It’s a double ensemble with a lot of story that we’re telling, and so I think we’ve gotten pretty good or comfortable kind of operating a at a certain pace and a certain kind of grammar, for lack of a better word, and so that was what we did,” he added. Watch on Deadline

As Nickerson explained it was an “incredible gift” to know they were ending after Season 4, Lyle noted that they were “reinvigorated” to get to return to civilization, which had always been their plan for the final season.

“We had been looking forward to that for so long now. It was part of the original pitch, and to finally get there—everything, when you’re pitching a show, it all feels like a pipe dream,” said Lyle. “You don’t think you’re actually going to be able to do any of this, especially something that you know is only gonna be if you get a first season, a second season, a third season. So, to actually reach that point and get to dive in, it reinvigorated everybody.”

In Yellowjackets, a 1996 New Jersey soccer team’s plane crashes in the Canadian wilderness, where they struggle to survive while they’re stranded for 19 months as a dark supernatural force seemingly lurks in the woods. Meanwhile, their adult counterparts cope with the memories of what went down in the wilderness.

With new episodes available to stream Fridays on Paramount+ with Premium Plan, the fourth and final season sees the Yellowjackets rescued and returned home, where they must adjust to civilization and take their secrets to the grave.

#3241. I’m a Deals Writer, and These Are My Top 10 Tech Deals This Week

As Lifehacker's deals writer, I'm always looking for the best bargains on TVs, speakers, laptops, and other tech. Now that it's Friday, I've rounded up this week's sales highlights.

This week, you can already feel the early Black Friday deals heating up with the sale starting next week. Amazon has many tech deals, as do Costco, Walmart, and other retailers. You can find price cuts on the M5 MacBook Air, the best headphones of 2026, Kindle readers, and more.

The Sony WH-1000XM6 are one of the best premium headphones of 2026, and right now, Amazon is offering them with a 24% on them right now. That brings the price of the Sony WH-1000XM6 headphones down to $348. You're not likely to see these headphones drop any further in price anytime soon, even with Black Friday coming up. So if you've had your eyes on the XM6, this is likely the best deal you'll get for a while.

The Kindle Paperwhite is having one of its best discounts right now, dropping to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. It's available in standard black, Jade, or Raspberry colors. This is the classic, standard e-reader from Amazon, but since it's not the Signature Edition, you'll have to put up with ads and the minimum 16GB storage (which still gets you storage for over a thousand e-books). There are other e-readers on sale as well if you want to see other options.

The MacBook Air with the M5 chip comes in both 13-inch and 15-inch sizes, and if you're interested in either, it's a good time to buy: Amazon is selling both right now at a $250 discount. That brings the 13-inch MacBook Air to $1,049.99 (down from $1,299) and the 15-inch MacBook Air to $1,249 (originally $1,499), reaching their lowest prices since the June price hikes.

Bose’s second-generation QuietComfort Headphones are down to $199 from $359, saving you $160 and bringing them to their lowest price yet. Weighing around 8.1 ounces, they’re among the lightest premium noise-canceling headphones, with generously padded earcups and a cushioned headband that spreads pressure without gripping too tightly. They’re also easy to pack for travel, as the earcups fold and swivel for storage in the included hard-shell carrying case.

The Bose SoundLink Plus hasn’t been on the market for long, but it’s already earned strong reviews—CNET labeled it “the Goldilocks of Bose Bluetooth speakers,” and it’s down to $179 (originally $269). This is a great opportunity to snatch a quality portable speaker with a big discount.

Amazon has cut the price of its latest Fire TV Stick 4K, dropping it to $19.99 from $59.99 and bringing it to its lowest price ever. At this price, it's an affordable way to bring 4K streaming to an older television or give a sluggish smart TV a performance upgrade.

The Sony WH-CH730N are $98 (originally $179), the lowest price they've ever been. They use the same Sony Connect app as the premium headphones; as a result, you get a 10-band slider on the EQ menu, a battery care feature that extends the longevity of your battery life, 50 hours of juice, ANC, Ambient Sound (transparency mode), Multipoint to connect to two devices at once, and Bluetooth 6.0.

Samsung’s HW-Q600F soundbar is down to $379.99 at Amazon from $499.99, a $120 discount that brings it to its lowest price ever. This 2025 model sits in the middle of Samsung’s Q-Series lineup and pairs a sleek, angular bar with a subwoofer in a 3.1.2 setup. Dolby Atmos also brings a modest sense of height, and effects track cleanly from left to right. You get a graphic equalizer and sound presets for adjusting the audio to your preferences through the included remote.

The Ultimate Ears Miniroll is down to $49.99 (originally $79.99), the second-lowest it has sold for so far. It’s a small, flat, puck-shaped Bluetooth speaker that weighs just over half a pound, with a removable rubber strap you can attach to a backpack, bike handlebar, or shower caddy. Despite its size, the Miniroll can get surprisingly loud—which PCMag confirms in its review—and at moderate volume, it has enough sound for a kitchen or backyard without sounding thin. As for its battery life, you get about 12 hours of playback before it needs a charge over USB-C, while its IP67 rating protects it from dust and a brief dunk in water.

If you're looking for a premium model, Samsung’s 65-inch S90H OLED TV is down to $1,397.99 from $2,697.99 at launch, saving you over $1,000. The sale price is easier to justify when you consider that this is a new 2026 model. If the 65-inch model does not suit your space, Samsung also sells the S90H in 42-, 48-, 55-, 77-, and 83-inch versions, and those sizes are discounted as well.

Apple is expected to release the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 sometime next spring. Ahead of that launch, new dummy units posted to social media today give us a closer look at the devices, including a big update to the iPhone Air 2.

9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

In a post on X, Sonny Dickson shared dummy units of the iPhone Air 2, giving us a glimpse of the new dual-camera system. Meanwhile, the base iPhone 18 looks largely unchanged compared to the iPhone 17.

The first-generation iPhone Air has a single 48MP Main camera. The second-generation model, however, will reportedly add an Ultra Wide camera.

First look at the iPhone 18 Air and iPhone 18 dummy units. The biggest change is the iPhone 18 Air, which now features two rear cameras instead of one, while the standard iPhone 18 retains a design similar to the iPhone 17. pic.twitter.com/MdOVuwPlm3

As expected, the iPhone Air 2 cameras are arranged horizontally across the pill-shaped camera plateau, similar to the iPhone Duo’s arrangement.

In addition to the dual-camera system, the iPhone Air 2 is expected to be powered by the A20 Pro chip. Apple is also reportedly working to improve the battery life. The Information has reported the device will feature a vapor chamber cooling system, which Apple debuted with the iPhone 17 Pro. Another report suggested the device will have a smaller Dynamic Island.

The base model iPhone 18, meanwhile, will reportedly use Apple’s A20 chip. Ming-Chi Kuo has reported it will have 9GB of RAM, up from the iPhone 17’s 8GB. It’s expected to be a modest year-over-year update, with Apple focused on cutting costs.

#3238. Sean Astin Mobilizes SAG-AFTRA In Fight For Universal Healthcare As “Substantial Majority” Of Members Don’t Qualify For Insurance

As many SAG-AFTRA members struggle to qualify for health insurance, the union is taking the issue to the U.S. government.

On Friday, Screen Actors Guild President Sean Astin announced the President’s Healthcare Task Force to address the “broken healthcare system” while several actors have faced losing their insurance under the union’s minimum eligibility requirements.

“This is a critical moment, where both our members and the public at large can no longer wait for relief from a broken healthcare system,” he said in a statement. “Our SAG-AFTRA Health Plan is healthy and strong, but a substantial majority of our members do not qualify. For our members who don’t qualify, there is very little that can be done to provide coverage.”

Astin added, “SAG-AFTRA has supported efforts to expand healthcare for all through the AFL-CIO. This task force seeks a new level of participation in the national movement to expand care for everyone. We will actively engage with policymakers, gather allies and provide a structured way for our members to participate formally in the process. The President’s Healthcare Task Force will be an instrument of support in the movement for universal healthcare.” Watch on Deadline

The SAG-AFTRA National Board voted unanimously on Friday to form the Task Force, which seeks to mobilize SAG-AFTRA’s collective strength and public influence to fight for universal access to affordable, comprehensive and reliable health care.

SAG’s new initiative comes amid financial scrutiny for the union following National Executive Director Duncan Crabtree-Ireland’s recent contract renewal, after his salary surpassed $1M in 2023.

#3237. iOS 27.3: New features, release date, more

iOS 27.3 is currently in beta testing with developers and public beta users. The update includes multiple new features for iPhone users, including the redesigned Health app, iPhone Duo updates, and much more. Here’s everything you need to know about what’s new in iOS 27.3 …

9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

As my colleague Ryan explained, Apple will likely release iOS 27.3 to all iPhone users sometime in December. Typically, Apple would release its x.2 software updates in December, but this year is different because iOS 27.1 was exclusive to iPhone Duo. That means that, in terms of the timeline, iOS 27.3 is essentially the equivalent of iOS 27.2.

Here’s when Apple has released its December updates in recent years:

So with that in mind, we expect iOS 27.3 to be released sometime during the first half of December.

The redesigned Health app is back in iOS 27.3. This was first available during testing of iOS 27.2, but did not ship as part of that final update.

The redesigned Health app is split into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The app features an all-new design that dynamically adapts based on your data, including Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab includes a new Health age feature that uses Apple Watch data to show how your metrics track relative to your actual age.

For Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 users, it also offers easy access to view your Readiness score every morning.

For Apple Fitness+, iOS 27.3 adds a new Gym Strength feature. This creates progressive, four-week plans based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment.

As you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weights you logged.

For iPhone Duo users, iOS 27.3 adds Reachability support. This setting shifts the interface on the outer display to the right or left, making it easier to reach the far corners. It’s designed to make iPhone Duo easier to use with one hand, despite the wider outer display. You activate it by swiping right on the right edge of the screen or left on the left edge.

Reachability for iPhone Duo is on by default. You can turn it off in Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

iOS 27.3 also brings a new face unlock feature to iPhone Duo. This is not full-fledged Face ID. Instead, Apple is using the front-facing camera on the iPhone Duo’s outer display to recognize you, then unlock the device. It doesn’t work for things like Apple Pay and passwords.

iOS 27.3 also tweaks the iPhone Duo’s software keyboard by making the keys slightly narrower and the font slightly smaller.

Finally, iOS 27.3 includes a new option in the Settings app to have your iPhone Duo lock when closed. Once enabled, your iPhone Duo will lock when you fold it, rather than transition content from the inner display to the outer display.

When it debuted, the iPhone Duo included a more robust version of StandBy with new clock faces and expanded customization options. iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s StandBy experience to all iPhone models.

This includes the redesigned Analog and Digital Clock faces, as well as additional customization options for colors and complications. The update also adds support for Shared Albums to the Photos face.

iOS 27.3 brings several key Siri AI updates. First, the update expands Siri AI with many new capabilities across Apple apps. Apple explains:

We started rolling out these new capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so users can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year.

There are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

With iOS 27.3, Apple is also starting to test new ways for developers to create Siri AI integrations for the first time. This is described as an “early Developer Preview.” Apple explains:

Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.

While this is being tested as part of iOS 27.3, Apple says it will start shipping to customers in a few months.

iOS 27.3 also expands Siri AI to new languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

iOS 27.3 also introduces usage limits on select Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features. The limits apply to things like:

You can unlock higher usage limits with an eligible iCloud+ plan, starting at $2.99 per month. If you hit your usage limit, basic Siri requests will still work. That includes things like setting timers and alarms.

#3232. How Microcredentials Can Help Engineers Build Trustworthy AI

IEEE Credentialing Program pairs AI governance standards with microcredentials

Kaitlyn Ridel is the IEEE microcredentials marketing specialist.

Engineering teams are moving at breakneck speed to integrate artificial intelligence, but they are running into a formidable new barrier: compliance issues. Translating high-level AI ethics, governance, and auditing into daily operational workflows has become one of the industry’s toughest challenges.

“AI ethics” refers to the principles developers use to govern and operate workflows. “Governance” refers to the rules and procedures an organization establishes for AI workflows and how they interact with organizational data. Auditing is the process of assessing and validating systems to ensure safety, fairness, transparency, and legal compliance.

Technology leads and systems engineers are responsible for adhering to a structured set of guidelines for standards and processes usually issued by a governing body such as the European Union, the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, and the International Organization for Standardization.

The regulations aim to mitigate issues such as systemic bias, security vulnerabilities, and transparency risks, but they also highlight a critical skills gap.

Most traditional computer science, software, and electrical engineering degree programs were built around technical design and system architecture. They do not yet include training in AI auditing, data tracking, or safety protocols for how AI systems interact with people and other technologies.

Expecting mid-career engineers to leave their job to attend a full-time two- or four-year program to learn about the topics is not feasible. Yet treating safety and governance as an afterthought can lead to costly product delays, legal exposure, and broken public trust.

Targeted microcredential programs can bridge the knowledge gap by helping engineers build skills in compliance, AI ethics, and governance.

Skills-based microcredentials represent the mastery of expertise gained through a learning program. To earn them, learners must demonstrate the skill through a validation assessment. The microcredentials can be stacked, showing a growing skill set in a defined area and allowing learners to earn several microcredentials in one program.

Microcredentials also allow engineers to upskill and master critical competencies, such as bias mitigation, algorithmic transparency, and risk auditing, without interrupting their career. Through rigorous skills-validation assessments, microcredentials give tech leaders verifiable proof that their teams can audit systems effectively before deployment.

For engineering organizations, microcredentialing creates an agile upskilling pathway. It connects software engineering and hardware design directly to regulatory frameworks, empowering teams to certify systems for safety and compliance within their development life cycles.

Bridging technical capability and ethical responsibility requires a trusted foundation. IEEE has long been a pioneer in socio-technical standards, most notably through the IEEE 7000 series for ethics in AI system design, a framework created to address ethical considerations during the development life cycle.

The IEEE Credentialing Program translates the organization’s world-class standards into actionable, industry-aligned microcredentials. For more than three decades, IEEE has set the gold standard for technical validation and professional certification. By pairing cutting-edge AI governance standards with targeted microcredential programs, IEEE provides engineers and IT leaders with clear, standardized road maps to build systems that are not just technically advanced but also safe, compliant, and worthy of public trust.

To learn more about the credentialing program, explore the offerings or connect with an IEEE expert.

Kaitlyn Ridel is a marketing specialist for the IEEE Microcredentialing Program

#3230. Apple’s ‘just works’ approach is great, but goes a little too far

“It just works” is one of the phrases most commonly associated with Apple. Interestingly, it appears to have been coined by the company’s customers and then used by reviewers before it was later picked up by Steve Jobs.

Of course, it’s now commonly used ironically when Apple products don’t do what they are supposed to (Apple Home, I’m looking at you), but I do think that it’s absolutely the right philosophy and goal – most of the time …

Macworld referenced an Apple brochure from 1996 entitled “Why do people prefer Macintosh?” This is a collection of testimonials from customers, a number of whom use the “it just works” phrasing. It was subsequently used by a number of reviewers. The earliest example I can find of Steve Jobs adopting it was in 1999, when discussing the rollout of FireWire to the Mac in the PowerMac G3.

It’s hot-pluggable. You don’t have to turn your computer off to connect and disconnect peripherals, you can just plug them right in. Again, the drivers are dynamically loaded. There are no terminators and there are no switches. It just works.

(If you have a link to any earlier example, please do let me know in the comments.)

I’m a big fan of the philosophy. Most of the time, users should just be able to get on with the tasks they want to execute without having to worry about the technology. The tech that makes it all possible should sit there quietly in the background.

However, there are cases where I think Apple takes this approach a little too far, and where tech-savvy users at least would like a little more transparency and control.

AirPods firmware updates are a good example. Back in September, there was quite a significant update in the form of custom EQ. It’s a rather basic version, but still a feature many had wanted for a long time. Instead of being able to manually trigger the update, users had to wait until it “just worked.”

Apple’s support document has a how-to guide that is essentially an outline of the conditions required to permit an update, and an instruction to simply wait until it happens. Which you will only know by repeatedly checking.

Make sure your AirPods are connected via Bluetooth to your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Connect your charging case to a power source. Put your AirPods in their charging case and close the lid. Keep the lid of the charging case closed, and keep your AirPods in Bluetooth range of your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Wait at least 30 minutes for the firmware to be updated. Check the firmware version again.

Another example, and one I’ve complained about before, is that there is no way to manually trigger an iCloud document sync, nor any progress indicator when it does finally happen. In the best of cases, it takes seconds; in the worst, many hours. And again, the only way to find out is to repeatedly check.

It’s the same story when shooting a video on your iPhone. Will it still be there an hour later, available to instantly edit and view? Maybe, or maybe it will have been offloaded to the cloud, requiring it to be downloaded before you can do anything with it – while a video you shot months earlier is still stored locally on the device! You can, of course, switch off optimization altogether, but if you choose to use it, you get no control over it. I want a setting that allows me to do things like specify local retention of all photos and videos taken within the past fortnight.

Will that video be available in the Mac Photos app when you check half an hour later? Maybe, maybe not. You can click the Sync Now button as many times as you like, and it will apparently have no effect, claiming it’s up to date despite the video being entirely absent. It will be there when it’s there.

Once it is in the Photos app on your Mac, it’s a similar story when exporting it to a folder. You can drag and drop the video into the folder, and this time you are manually triggering the transfer (yay!), but there will be absolutely no visual indication that it is in progress. No grayed-out icon, no progress bar, nothing. So far as the user interface is concerned, it appears that your drag and drop had no effect – until the video file finally appears.

I think with all of these things and more, Apple needs to offer options. Yes, most non-tech users may be perfectly happy to just wait until things happen, but there ought to be a standard way to trigger things that currently happen in their own sweet time, as well as progress indicators and confirmation that a process is complete.

Is this an ecosystem-wide improvement you’d like to see? Please share your thoughts in the comments and add any frustrating examples of your own.

#3229. 28 Zero-Day Findings in Under Two Days. Is Robotics Security Keeping Pace?

VicOne’s AI-assisted research reveals what faster zero-day discovery means for robot safety

VicOne is a Physical AI cybersecurity company protecting vehicles and robots from cyber threats that can alter behavior and compromise safety.

VicOne used AI to find 28 zero-day vulnerabilities in Physical AI tools —these weaknesses can impact robot training, testing, and real-world control.

This article is brought to you by VicOne.

VicOne identified an initial set of 28 zero-day findings in less than two days using AI-assisted research across software and tools supporting the Physical AI ecosystem. These include projects developed or maintained by Google, NVIDIA, and Meta, among others.

Based on initial validation, all 28 findings are classified as zero-day vulnerabilities. The count may change following vendor and vulnerability-authority review, and some findings do not yet have CVE tracking numbers.

Many of these tools help teams train, simulate, test, and operate robots. Weaknesses in them could influence the models teams build, the test results they trust, and the instructions sent to robots.

These findings create two demands for robotics teams: responding as AI helps uncover weaknesses faster, and assessing how each one could affect robot safety and operations.

Vulnerability discovery involves examining code, tracing how systems communicate, and testing whether a suspected weakness can actually be exploited. AI can accelerate parts of this work, helping researchers analyze more software in less time. Attackers could use similar capabilities.

When the weakness is a zero-day — previously unknown and without an available fix — faster discovery can leave teams with little time to respond. While that exposure does not necessarily mean an attack has occurred, teams still need to determine whether they use the affected software and what an attacker could access or change.

VicOne’s findings span three stages of the robotics lifecycle: development and training, simulation and validation, and deployment and runtime. Weaknesses at each stage could affect what a robot learns, how it is tested, and how it is controlled.

Figure 1. In this research set, 75% of findings involved development, training, simulation, or validation tools, highlighting risks that can arise before a robot is deployed.VicOne

The following scenarios show how a compromised component could influence the robot at each stage.

These are potential consequences and not demonstrated outcomes for every finding. Actual effects depend on the attacker’s access, the system’s design, and whether other safeguards prevent the changes from reaching physical behavior.

In a separate demonstration, VicOne researchers provide a concrete example of a weakness affecting a protective function. The researchers exploited a vulnerability to prevent a robot’s remote-stop command from working. The case shows why teams need to test whether safeguards remain effective when the software supporting them is compromised.

Video 1. VicOne researchers demonstrate a vulnerability that prevents a robot’s remote-stop command from working. VicOne

AI can shorten the search for weaknesses, but a robotics team still needs to determine whether a fix is safe to deploy. Even after a software maintainer releases a patch, teams must identify affected systems, check compatibility, and verify that the update preserves intended behavior.

An earlier successful test remains useful evidence. However, a newly discovered weakness may reveal conditions that test never examined.

When immediate updating is impractical, teams may need temporary safeguards, such as restricting access to an affected service, while a validated fix is prepared.

As details from the 28 findings become available through coordinated disclosure, the next step is for robotics manufacturers is to connect each finding to its potential effect on development, deployment, and robot behavior.

That work also requires understanding how threats could affect robot behavior and how to protect systems already in operation. VicOne Radeis helps teams identify potential zero-day vulnerabilities, assess AI model and system security, and use simulation to evaluate how these risks could affect robot behavior before deployment. VicOne Rthena supports threat detection and responses within approved policies during operation.

Figure 2. Cybersecurity strengthens robot safety evidence throughout the lifecycle. VicOne helps teams test safety limits against manipulation before deployment and monitor the conditions behind safe behavior in operation.VicOne

Faster vulnerability discovery matters when teams can turn findings into action: identify what needs attention, verify that safeguards still hold, and confirm that a fix does not introduce new risks. That is how cybersecurity strengthens robot safety as systems continue to change.

For a deeper look how cybersecurity can affect robot safety, download our white paper, “Why Robot Safety Depends on Cybersecurity: Protecting the Information That Safety Decisions Rely On.”

#3227. Apple Calendar got two feature upgrades it really needed in iOS 27

Apple Calendar keeps getting better, including some design updates coming in iOS 27.3. But there are two standout feature upgrades added recently in iOS 27 that Apple’s Calendar app really needed.

I’ve used Apple’s Calendar app for years, and there’s an elegant simplicity to it. But one key area the app has long lagged behind competitors is event creation.

When you need to create a new event, the Calendar app historically has required manually filling in various fields for the title, date, time, invitees, etc. By contrast, the excellent third-party app Fantastical lets you type in natural language and it automatically fills in relevant parameters based on what you type.

In iOS 27, Apple finally introduces its own natural language input for Calendar events. You can type out your event details and certain recognized parameters will be used to automatically fill in the detail fields.

While the feature still isn’t on par with what Fantastical offers, since it doesn’t support as many data points as the third-party alternative, it’s very much a step in the right direction.

Apple has always pitched Siri as being like a personal assistant. As such, calendar-related tasks should have been Siri’s strong suit. But until iOS 27, you couldn’t actually manage your calendar very well using Siri.

With Siri AI, that’s changed in a big way. Now, you can do things like:

One of my favorite personal examples is from this summer when the NFL schedule was released. I asked Siri to find the Dallas Cowboys schedule and add every game to my calendar, and it pulled this off with ease.

Siri is so much better than before at assisting with your calendar, and iOS 27.3 will bring even more capabilities soon.

What are your favorite iOS 27 Apple Calendar upgrades? Let us know in the comments.

#3225. Advanced Metrology for Defect Detection, Tool Health, and Semiconductor Yield Enhancement



In advanced semiconductor manufacturing, small defects can have a large effect on yield. Thin film deposition tools must stay stable and qualified. Process drift must be caught early. When a defect does appear, engineers need to know where it came from and how it affects device performance. This webinar shows how in-line inspection and offline characterization combine into one workflow, from tool monitoring to root-cause analysis.

In the first half, Dr. Bitan Chakraborty from Intel, explains how surface scan metrology fits into station monitors for thin film tools. The session shows how baseline signatures and real-time monitoring reveal hardware wear, particle generation, and process drift before they reach production wafers. It then moves to in-line scans on patterned wafers. These scans expose layer-level defects and show how they form and spread through multi-layer device stacks. Linking this defect data to electrical test results helps teams find root causes and focus their yield improvement work.

In the second half, Dr. Jacob Petersen from Evident Scientific, addresses a common question: what happens after an in-line tool flags a problem? In-line tools are fast, but they cannot always provide the details needed for a firm conclusion. Offline 3D optical profilometry fills that gap by combining three complementary inspection techniques in a single system. It delivers dimensional measurements and helps determine whether a defect lies within the sample or comes from foreign material. The session covers how several optical techniques support inspection from bare silicon to fully packaged chips. It also shows how automation enables fast measurement of features down to the sub-nanometer scale with minimal operator handling.

What You Will Learn:

  • How surface scan metrology in station monitors tracks tool health and supports the qualification of thin film deposition processes
  • How baseline signatures and real-time monitoring detect particle generation, hardware degradation, and process drift before production is affected
  • How in-line scans on patterned wafers reveal layer-level defects and show how they propagate through multi-layer device structures
  • When offline 3D optical profilometry should follow in-line inspection, and how it measures dimensions and separates sample defects from foreign material
  • How correlating tool health data, inspection results, and electrical performance links physical defects to yield loss and guides targeted improvement projects

#3223. Shopify vs. Uber Technologies: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy?

Shopify's revenue surge and Uber's free cash flow make for a sharp contrast, but one future opportunity may settle which stock to own.

By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 5:20PM EST

Choosing between Shopify (SHOP -6.25%) and Uber Technologies (UBER -3.25%) involves weighing two different tech stocks. Both companies have become essential to how we shop and move.

Shopify acts as the digital backbone for millions of online merchants, while Uber manages a massive logistics and transportation network. This comparison evaluates their financials and business models to see which is a better pick for 2027 and beyond.

Shopify provides the essential digital tools that allow companies to build their own online storefronts and manage physical retail locations. The company serves millions of merchants in multiple countries, providing an all-in-one ecosystem for everything from inventory management to payment processing. By focusing on giving brands total control over their customer relationships, it has become a central player among tech stocks that support the broader e-commerce market.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $14.2 billion, representing an increase of approximately 32.5% compared to the prior twelve-month period. This robust growth was accompanied by net income of $2.1 billion.

Uber Technologies operates a massive technology platform that connects people to transportation, food delivery, and logistics services. Its network spans over 70 countries, serving a growing number of monthly active consumers who use the app for ridesharing or ordering from local merchants. The company leverages partnerships with major retailers like Best Buy (BBY -1.33%) and Tractor Supply (TSCO -0.77%) to expand its reach beyond traditional restaurant delivery into a broader marketplace.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $56.5 billion, which is a growth rate of approximately 13.9% over the previous twelve months. The company generated net income of around $3.5 billion during this period.

Shopify faces intense market competition from established platforms and niche providers that could limit its growth or force pricing changes. The company depends heavily on third-party cloud infrastructure from Alphabet (GOOGL -2.70%) and payment processors like PayPal Holdings (PYPL -5.46%). New risks involve the use of artificial intelligence, which could lead to inaccurate outputs or regulatory challenges.

Uber Technologies deals with ongoing legal and regulatory challenges regarding how it classifies its drivers, which could fundamentally change its business model. It competes globally in mobility and delivery against well-capitalized rivals such as Lyft (LYFT -2.54%) and DoorDash (DASH -2.88%). The platform is also vulnerable to macroeconomic shifts, as inflation or rising fuel prices can impact consumer spending on rides and deliveries. Finally, the company relies on the mobile marketplaces of Apple (AAPL -1.90%) and Alphabet to reach its vast user base.

Uber Technologies appears more reasonably priced as it trades at a much lower forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio and price-to-sales (P/S) ratio than Shopify.

Both are well-run companies. But if I had to pick only one stock, it would be Uber. It's not so much about anything Shopify is doing wrong; it's more about Uber growing its current business and the opportunities ahead.

Despite Uber being a well-established brand, its recent 2026 third-quarter earnings results showed that monthly active users increased by 14% to 215 million. Trips also increased by 16% to 4.1 billion, and gross bookings climbed 20% to roughly $60 billion. That shows not only that more people are signing up to use its platform, but that users are also booking more rides and deliveries.

For its sales growth opportunities, the focus should be on robotaxis, which could be a huge market. According to research from Goldman Sachs (GS -6.71%), the global robotaxi market size is expected to reach $415 billion by 2035. By the end of 2026, Uber expects to have 700 fully driverless vehicles on its platform, with more than 2,000 in 2027.

Shopify will continue to benefit from the growth of e-commerce sales. But for long-term investors, understanding that the roads over the next decade will be filled with more autonomous vehicles, Uber can be a centerpiece in that market, which should only grow in value.

#3222. Signal now blocks screenshots on iPhone to stop Siri AI from seeing chats

Popular secure messaging app Signal has rolled out a new update that automatically disables screenshots for the sake of blocking Siri AI from reading your chats. Here are the details.

Signal’s latest app update on iPhone disables a key system feature: taking screenshots.

As Signal told Reuters, that’s because Apple doesn’t currently provide better tools for iOS developers to safeguard app content from Siri AI and third-party AI agents.

By default, users who update and try to take a screenshot will see a message that says: “Screenshot prevented by ‘Block Siri AI’ setting.”

Signal now blocks in-app screenshots on iPhone to keep Siri AI from reading chatsIt’s a new toggle in settings that’s on by default, but can be turned offNo equivalent for its Mac app pic.twitter.com/ImsinqMNPq

Here’s exactly what that toggle does, per the in-app settings:

Prevent Siri AI from scanning Signal content. This will also block you from taking screenshots in the app and App Switcher.

Apple already lets you block Siri AI from accessing whichever apps you manually exclude, and that became even easier in iOS 27.2. But rather than directing users to that system option, Signal seems to believe it needed to take action itself with this update.

#3220. Webull: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Acquiring Pi Securities gave Webull a foothold in Thailand, a move that tests whether its global platform can scale beyond U.S. retail.

By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 21, 2026 at 5:27PM EST

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 19, 2026, Webull (BULL -9.19%) announced record total revenue of $219 million, up 39% year over year. Client assets reached $32.4 billion during the period. Expanding operating margins show how higher user activity builds long-term earnings power. Three things management said stand out.

The relaxation of the pattern day trader, or PDT, rule in June removed day-trading limits on accounts under $25,000. Webull capitalized on this shift as options and equities trading from smaller accounts surged without dampening overall user retention.

Webull completed its acquisition of Pi Securities, a brokerage operating in Thailand, to accelerate its international expansion. The transaction added $3 billion in customer assets while expanding access to high-balance accounts in Thailand.

Management launched crypto perpetual futures (perps), which are derivative contracts allowing traders to speculate on asset prices without an expiration date. Adding these products diversifies revenue away from traditional equity trading and expands options for active traders.

Trading momentum continued through October across active retail accounts, and Webull is capturing market share in U.S. options. It relies on its global technology platform, multi-market compliance infrastructure, and product innovation to drive customer growth while maintaining expense discipline.

With international expansion and new asset classes scaling, leadership points to significant long-term runway across global markets.
